DEL-09-03 exists to make vNext runtime, lifecycle, dependency, attachment, and permission behavior testable at focused unit/API/integration levels.
The deliverable supports release readiness by expanding regression coverage for named behaviors rather than implementing those behaviors directly.

Test product-owned contracts not SDK defaults: assertions target AgentEnginePort, TurnEngine, browser UIEvents, canonical HarnessEvents, and permission decisions; SDK values belong only in adapter metadata assertions.
Preserve browser compatibility: `/api/harness/turn` tests should protect stable SSE event names and route shape while allowing runtime internals to move behind TurnEngine.
Make audit order observable: accepted-turn persistence, terminal outcomes, replay tolerance, and redaction should be asserted as ordered records where possible (CONTRACT K-EVENT-2 through K-EVENT-6).
Deny paths need first-class tests: denied writes, denied Bash, unknown tools, failed hooks, `dontAsk`, and `readOnly` are product-critical boundaries, not edge cases.
Fixture design should expose failure mode: attachment, dependency, status, and JSONL fixtures should be small, named by failure condition, and reusable across unit/API tests.
Prefer narrow tests around a single invariant when the invariant is explicitly source-defined, such as `_STATUS.md` forward-only transitions or `Dependencies.csv` required columns.
Use integration tests when behavior depends on route cleanup, session locking, SSE termination, cancellation, or multiple services.
Use unit tests for deterministic parsers, mappers, permission resolution, fixture validation, and event replay.
Keep Section 9 validation IDs aligned with DEL-09-02; authoring the runner/ID catalog belongs to DEL-09-02 unless a later human ruling changes scope.
Mark unimplemented or phase-dependent coverage as TBD or ASSUMPTION rather than creating tests that assert unavailable behavior.
Treat missing implementation paths, fixture paths, and command output as closure evidence gaps, not permission to invent paths.
Broad matrix vs focused regression: favor source-mapped regression cases for named DEL-09-03 behaviors; defer exhaustive cross-product matrices unless a source requirement demands them.

Mocked engine vs real SDK adapter: use stubs for deterministic product-owned contract tests; use SDK-backed adapter tests only where the source requirement is adapter conformance or Provider/SDK message mapping.
API route tests vs service tests: keep route tests focused on request validation, locking, SSE encoding, cleanup, and stable shape; put runtime policy assertions in TurnEngine/permission/event tests.
Current vs future phase behavior: tests for future phase behavior should be pending/TBD or fixture-ready until the corresponding implementation deliverable lands.

Minimum coverage vs unavailable surfaces: require one implemented or explicitly deferred test decision per DEL-09-03 behavior group, keeping future-phase surfaces TBD until the owning implementation exists.

DEL-09-03 shall define and implement focused unit, API, and integration test expansion for TurnEngine, SSE compatibility, event replay, attachment validation, status lifecycle, dependency register behavior, interrupts/cancellation, and denied actions.
The deliverable excludes feature implementation except test fixtures and packaging glue, and shall not create or populate `Dependencies.csv` during the four-document initialization run.

DEL-09-03-REQ-001: tests shall cover `TurnEngine.runTurn()` as a product-owned lifecycle boundary separate from HTTP route ownership; unit tests exercise TurnEngine without HTTP and assert accepted-turn persistence, event yield, terminal outcomes, and adapter boundary behavior.

DEL-09-03-REQ-002: tests shall preserve `/api/harness/turn` SSE route compatibility including stable browser event names session:init, chat:delta, chat:complete, tool:result, session:complete, turn:error, and process:exit.
DEL-09-03-REQ-003: tests shall verify accepted user input is persisted before SDK/model execution begins, asserting `turn.accepted` precedes model/request execution records (CONTRACT K-EVENT-2).
DEL-09-03-REQ-004: tests shall verify every accepted turn reaches a durable terminal success, failure, cancellation, or interruption event (CONTRACT K-EVENT-3).
DEL-09-03-REQ-005: tests shall cover append-only HarnessEvent JSONL replay including malformed trailing line tolerance and preservation of valid prior events (SPEC Section 9.2; CONTRACT K-EVENT-5).

DEL-09-03-REQ-006: tests shall verify attachment resolver enforcement for path validation, regular-file status, symlink rejection, extension allowlist, readability, per-file 10 MB limit, total raw-byte 18 MB limit, partial failure, and all-failure empty-text rejection (SPEC Section 16.1; CONTRACT K-ATTACH-1).

DEL-09-03-REQ-007: tests shall verify `_STATUS.md` parsing and forward-only lifecycle transition enforcement, including approval SHA requirements for CHECKING and ISSUED (SPEC Section 4; PRD FR-052 through FR-054).

DEL-09-03-REQ-008: tests shall verify `Dependencies.csv` v3.1 parsing, validation, writing, provenance preservation, host deliverable consistency, row retirement, and legacy normalization (SPEC Section 6; PRD FR-055 through FR-057).

DEL-09-03-REQ-009: tests shall verify denied actions do not execute and emit permission/runtime events where supported, covering deny-over-allow, `dontAsk`, `readOnly`, unknown tool names, denied writes, denied Bash, and hook failure (SPEC Sections 14-15; CONTRACT K-PERM-1 through K-PERM-5, K-BASH-1).
DEL-09-03-REQ-010: tests shall keep public APIs and canonical events provider-neutral, with SDK-specific names and IDs only as adapter metadata (SPEC Section 10.3; PRD FR-122 and FR-123).

DEL-09-03-REQ-011: closure shall include at least one implemented or explicitly deferred test case for each of the eight required behavior groups, recording any uncovered group as TBD, deferred, or blocked with source-backed rationale.

DEL-09-03-REQ-012: closure shall preserve stable validation evidence for `npm run test` after implementation paths are selected; command evidence remains TBD until execution occurs (CONTRACT K-VALIDATE-1; PRD Section 12.2; SPEC Section 19.1).
